ex.en: I can't stand this heat.
These shoes will hold up for a long time.
Hang in there a little longer and it's the weekend.

en: to disturb, interrupt, get in the way
note: 방해가 되다 = to be a bother.

ex.en: Don't disturb me when I'm studying.
Sorry to interrupt. Do you have a minute?
The noise from the next table is interrupting our conversation.
My hands get rough in winter.
This towel is a bit rough.
That person talks a bit harshly.
The dishes have really piled up.
A lot of stress has built up lately.
A lot of snow piled up overnight.

note: 구멍이 나다 = to get a hole.

ex.en: I got a hole in my sock.
I got a flat tire, so I was late.

ex.s: 벨트에 구멍을 하나 더 뚫어 주세요.
ex.en: Please punch one more hole in the belt.

ex.s: 우리 가족은 밥 먹기 전에 기도해요.
ex.en: Our family prays before eating.
I'll pray that the surgery goes well.
Grandma prays every morning.
I never imagined that.

ex.s: 이 집에 사는 걸 상상해 보세요.
ex.en: Imagine living in this house.
Kids have such big imaginations.

note: 걱정하다 = to worry; 걱정되다 = to feel worried.

ex.en: Don't worry.
I'm really worried about the exam.
Thanks for worrying about me.
That movie comes out next week.
Drink opened milk soon.
I took a photo before opening the package.
I got a call in the middle of a meeting.
It rained on my way home.
Sorry for getting up in the middle of the meal.

note: 안마하다 = to massage. 마사지 is also common.

ex.en: Could you rub my shoulders?

ex.s: 아버지 생신 선물로 안마 의자를 샀어요.
ex.en: We bought a massage chair for Dad's birthday.
I got a massage after working out.
I built muscle from working out.
My muscles are sore from moving yesterday.
I stretch to loosen up my muscles.

note: 완전히 = completely. Casual 완전 = totally (완전 맛있어요).

ex.en: My cold is completely gone.
This plan isn't complete yet.
Nobody's perfect.
I passed my driving test!
My daughter got into the college she wanted.
If I pass the interview, I start work next month.

note: Opposite: 전반 (first half). 초반 = early part.

ex.en: He's in his late twenties.
They scored in the second half of the soccer game.
I'm going on vacation late next month.

note: Somewhat formal; 사람을 쓰다 is casual.

ex.en: The store hired two part-timers.
We hired people to help when we moved.
Should I hire a lawyer?

note: 편하다 is the shorter, more common form.

ex.en: This sofa is really comfortable.
Come wearing comfortable shoes.
I feel at ease when I'm with him.

en: to take care of, look after

ex.en: I have to look after my nephew this weekend.

ex.s: 휴가 동안 고양이 좀 돌봐 줄 수 있어요?
ex.en: Can you look after my cat while I'm on vacation?
The nurse took good care of the patient.
My nephew is already ten.
I came to buy a birthday present for my niece.
I video-called my niece.
That plan isn't very realistic.

ex.s: 현실적으로 이번 달은 여행 못 가요.
ex.en: Realistically, I can't travel this month.

ex.s: 좀 더 현실적인 가격을 말해 주세요.
ex.en: Please give me a more realistic price.

note: Noun 계획 (plan) is very common: 계획 있어요?

ex.s: 이번 여름에 제주도 여행을 계획하고 있어요.
ex.en: We're planning a trip to Jeju this summer.
We secretly planned Mom's birthday party.

ex.s: 다음 주 일정을 미리 계획해 두세요.
ex.en: Plan next week's schedule ahead of time.
It's an honor to meet you.
It's an honor to work with you.
I'm honored you invited me to the wedding.

ex.s: 그 밴드가 다음 달에 서울에서 공연해요.
ex.en: That band is performing in Seoul next month.
The kids performed a play at school.
What time is this musical playing?
Shall I carry your bags for you?

ex.s: 이사 때문에 아직 짐을 싸고 있어요.
ex.en: I'm still packing for the move.
I don't want to be a burden to my family.
Today is truly the worst day.
That restaurant's service was the worst.
Worst case, we can just take a taxi.
A winter this warm is rare.

ex.s: 그 사람이 늦는 건 드문 일이에요.
ex.en: It's rare for him to be late.

ex.s: 요즘 편지를 손으로 쓰는 사람은 드물어요.
ex.en: People who write letters by hand are rare these days.
Get regular health checkups.
We get together regularly to play soccer.
The regular meeting is on Monday.
I recovered quickly after the surgery.

ex.s: 푹 자면 체력을 회복할 수 있어요.
ex.en: A good night's sleep will restore your energy.

ex.s: 두 사람은 관계를 회복하려고 노력하고 있어요.
ex.en: The two of them are trying to repair their relationship.
Anything's fine with me.
It doesn't matter if it rains.
That has nothing to do with this.
I eat fruit in the morning.
I'll go buy some fruit at the market.
What fruit do you like best?

note: 반지를 끼다 = put on; 빼다 = take off.

ex.en: I lost my wedding ring.

ex.s: 이 반지 한번 껴 봐도 돼요?
ex.en: Can I try on this ring?
I take off my ring when I do the dishes.
The nurse called my name.
My younger sibling is a nurse.
Nurses who work night shifts have it really hard.

note: 존중받다 = to be respected. 존경하다 = to look up to.

ex.en: We should respect each other's opinions.
My parents respected my decision.
Kids want to be respected too.
Keep the leftovers in the fridge.

ex.s: 짐을 호텔에 잠깐 보관할 수 있어요?
ex.en: Can I leave my bags at the hotel for a bit?
Be sure to keep the receipt.
We went to a strawberry farm on the weekend.
My uncle runs a farm in the countryside.
These eggs came from a nearby farm.

note: Often 때로는. 가끔 is more casual.

ex.en: Sometimes I want to be alone.
This road sometimes gets really backed up.
Sometimes you need to rest, too.

note: 체험하다 = to experience firsthand. 경험 = experience in general.

ex.en: The kids went on a farm visit with their school.

ex.s: 한복 입기 체험을 해 보고 싶어요.
ex.en: I want to try wearing hanbok.
The free trial period ended.

note: ㄹ-drop: 떠는. 떨리다 = to feel shaky/nervous.

ex.en: I was shivering from the cold.
Please stop bouncing your leg.
I chatted with my friends all night.

note: 러-irregular: 푸르러요. Covers both blue and green.

ex.en: The sky is really blue today.
Now that it's spring, the mountains have turned green.
I want to see the blue sea.
I can't be bothered to cook today.
Sorry to bother you.
Typing my password every time is a hassle.

note: Often means an online forum or group.

ex.en: I get a lot of info from a parenting forum.
I posted a question in a gaming community.
I bought a used chair through the neighborhood community.
I'm getting up early tomorrow no matter what.

ex.s: 여기 오면 무조건 이 메뉴를 시켜요.
ex.en: Whenever I come here, I always order this.

ex.s: 아이 말을 무조건 다 들어주면 안 돼요.
ex.en: You shouldn't give in to everything a kid wants.
A tree fell over because of the wind.
Grandpa collapsed on the street.
I was so tired I crashed as soon as I got home.
He has a good sense of style.
It's so cold I can't feel my fingers.
I haven't played tennis in a while, so I've lost my touch.
Please divide the cake equally.
I think the same way.
Please cut it the same as last time.

note: 균형을 잡다 = to keep one's balance.

ex.en: Work-life balance is important.

ex.s: 자전거 탈 때 균형 잡기가 어려워요.
ex.en: It's hard to keep my balance on a bike.
Eat balanced meals.
What's the total amount?
Please double-check the amount.
I typed the wrong amount to send to my friend.

note: 땀이 나다 = to sweat; 땀을 흘리다 = to drip sweat.

ex.en: I sweated a lot from working out.
It's so hot I'm sweating.
I sweat when I eat spicy food.
Sprinkle a little salt on the meat.
I put on perfume before going out.
Spray on bug repellent before you go camping.

note: 대답하다 = to answer (a person). 답 = answer (to a problem).

ex.en: Please answer my question.
I sent a text, but there's no reply.
My kid won't answer when I call him.
The bus is really shaky.
This table wobbles a bit.
The leaves are swaying in the wind.
I didn't expect it to be this expensive.
I expect the meeting to take a long time.
We arrived sooner than I expected.

note: 불만이 있다 = to be unhappy with something.

ex.en: The customer says they're unhappy with the service.
If you have any complaints, please tell me.
The kids complain a lot about school lunches.

note: 피아노를 치다 = to play the piano.

ex.en: I learned piano as a kid.
My daughter practices piano every day.
This café has a piano.

ex.s: 우리 아기는 우리의 가장 큰 기쁨이에요.
ex.en: Our baby is our greatest joy.

ex.s: 합격 소식을 듣고 기쁨의 눈물을 흘렸어요.
ex.en: I cried tears of joy when I heard I passed.
I find joy in little things.
That jacket is really cool.
The view here is really great.
Dad looked cool cooking.
Did you save the file?

ex.s: 사진이 너무 많아서 저장 공간이 부족해요.
ex.en: I have so many photos that I'm out of storage.
I saved the recipe to look at later.

note: 표 is the native word, also common.

ex.en: I bought concert tickets.
Plane tickets are so expensive.
You can just show your ticket on your phone.
This bag is a summer must-have.
I bought a new item in the game.
Do you have a good business idea?
What department are you in?
I had dinner with friends from my department.
There's an alum from my department at my company.
I spilled soup on my clothes at the restaurant.
My kid spilled milk on the floor.
I poured a lot of time into this project.
The explanation is so confusing.
The subway lines were complicated, so I was confused.
My head's been a bit of a mess lately.
Plastic destroys the environment.
The typhoon destroyed the village.
I destroyed the enemy base in the game.
Thanks for last time.
I went to Busan last week.
I'll have what I had last time.
Mark the important parts.
I marked the hotel's location on the map.
I marked Mom's birthday on the calendar.
I bought a lot of boxes for the move.
Could I get just one box?
I put the birthday gift in a pretty box.
I'm sure I put it here, but it's gone.
He'll definitely be late.
They definitely said it'll rain tomorrow.
My kid is afraid of the dark.
I turned on my phone's light in the dark.
Wait until your eyes adjust to the dark.

note: Formal-ish; 물건 is the everyday word.

ex.en: Please put your personal items in the locker.
We're out of office supplies.
We're collecting items to donate.
Parking is limited to two hours.
This event has limited spots.

ex.s: 아이 휴대폰 사용 시간이 제한돼 있어요.
ex.en: My kid's phone time is limited.
I clean the house every weekend.
Please clean your room.
I clean before closing the shop.
My younger sister is pregnant.
How many months pregnant are you?

ex.s: 임신 중에는 이 약을 먹으면 안 돼요.
ex.en: You shouldn't take this medicine while pregnant.
I'm not getting enough sleep lately.
I have a headache from lack of sleep.
I wore a sleep mask on the plane.

note: Usually 정상적으로 or 정상적인. 정상이에요 = it's normal.

ex.en: The elevator is working normally again.
They say the baby is growing normally.
The order went through normally.
Tax day is coming up soon.
Is tax included in this price?
A lot of tax comes out of my paycheck.

note: 숨 is the everyday word for breath.

ex.en: I got short of breath climbing the stairs.
Breathing is important when you do yoga.

ex.s: 그 두 사람은 호흡이 잘 맞아요.
ex.en: Those two work really well together.
I'd like to cancel my reservation.
We canceled camping because it rained.
Can I cancel my order?
Don't get me wrong.
There was a small misunderstanding.
I'm glad the misunderstanding was cleared up.
It's very cloudy today.
I looked down at the clouds from the plane.
My kid laughs at the shapes of the clouds.

note: 결제하다 = to pay. Don't confuse with 결재 (approval).

ex.en: I'll pay by card.
The online payment isn't going through.
You get a discount if you pay with the app.
Something urgent came up, so I'll head out first.
If you eat too fast, you'll get indigestion.
I really need the bathroom.

note: Formal; 시키다 is the everyday word.

ex.en: The team leader told me to rewrite the report.
Do as the teacher instructed.

ex.s: 의사가 지시한 대로 약을 먹고 있어요.
ex.en: I'm taking the medicine as the doctor instructed.
Try zooming in on the photo.
The company expanded its business overseas.

ex.s: 이 사진을 크게 확대해서 뽑아 주세요.
ex.en: Please print this photo enlarged.
Just kidding.
Dad often tells unfunny jokes.
We were in a meeting, so it wasn't the mood for jokes.

note: 체크하다 = to check. 체크카드 = debit card.

ex.en: What time is check-in?
Did you check off everything we need?
Please check your email.
It snowed, so everything is white.
I got tteokbokki sauce on my white shirt.
You look pale. Are you okay?

note: Formal; 좀 or 조금 in casual speech.

ex.en: The price is a bit high.
It's a bit chilly today.
The meeting ran a bit long.
At least let me know.

ex.s: 공항에 최소한 두 시간 전에 가세요.
ex.en: Get to the airport at least two hours early.
You should at least show basic manners.
Two cars collided on the highway.
We disagreed a lot while planning the wedding.
The meeting times conflict with each other.

note: 마스크를 쓰다 = to wear a mask.

ex.en: I wore a mask because I have a cold.
Be sure to wear a mask because of the fine dust.
I bought a mask at the convenience store.
He's a real gentleman.

ex.s: 그 사람이 신사답게 문을 열어 줬어요.
ex.en: He opened the door for me like a gentleman.
Ladies and gentlemen, welcome.
They say the new phone launches next month.
The company released a new flavor.
Our team launched a new app.
This bus route has changed.
Do you have a subway map?

ex.s: 새 지하철 노선이 집 근처에 생겨요.
ex.en: A new subway line is opening near my home.
The wedding date has been set.
The meeting time hasn't been finalized yet.
I'll let you know once the trip schedule is set.

note: 생존하다 = to survive; 살아남다 is more everyday.

ex.en: In this heat, AC is a matter of survival.
I watched a show about surviving on a desert island.

ex.s: 요즘 작은 가게들은 생존이 쉽지 않아요.
ex.en: Survival isn't easy for small shops these days.

note: 피 is the everyday word; 혈액 is medical.

ex.en: I have a blood test tomorrow.
What's your blood type?
Exercise improves blood circulation.

note: Formal (forms, official talk); 살다 in everyday speech.

ex.en: My parents live in Busan.
Many foreigners live in this apartment complex, too.
Please write your current address.
This cup keeps drinks hot or cold for a long time.
You have to exercise to stay healthy.
The Wi-Fi connection keeps dropping.
I support a children's charity every month.
This company sponsored the festival.
My parents paid for my studies abroad.
I bought my favorite singer's new album.
My father collects old records.

ex.s: 그 밴드가 다음 달에 음반을 내요.
ex.en: That band is putting out an album next month.
